How this works

  1. 1 Two observers, neither asked for a verdict. A language model is read for token probabilities only — how predictable each word was — and a second reference reads the same text. Neither is ever asked is this AI.
  2. 2 43 interpretable features. Those probabilities become named measurements: average predictability, log rank, rhythm of surprise, distance from applicant prose.
  3. 3 A calibrated probability whose logit is the explanation. The features are summed into log-odds. That sum is the reason — every number below is arithmetic you can check, not a judgement.

How much reads as machine-written

Confidence any of it is machine-written

These numbers are evidence, not a verdict. The tool has not cleared this essay and cannot: a low share means the evidence did not reach the threshold, not that a person wrote it.

Two different questions, kept apart on purpose. The left figure is how much of the essay carries the signal; the right is how sure the tool is that any of it does. A short polished passage inside honest writing moves the right number and barely touches the left.

What this tool gets wrong

Eight measured failure modes, shipped with every result. Read them before you act on anything above.

    Your essay is sent to a remote observer model to be scored, so it leaves your machine. Nothing is stored and nothing is used for training, but the request is real: treat the text as read by a third party.
